abstract: Mitochondrial membrane potential is the charge difference across the inner mitochondrial membrane that is generated by the electron transport chain pumping protons from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space and is required for ATP synthesis, importing proteins into the mitochondria and movement of ions across the inner mitochondrial membrane. While a number of long-lived genetic mutants in C. elegans have been reported to have reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, increased mitochondrial membrane potential has also been associated with increased longevity. In this work, we examined the role of mitochondrial membrane potential in the long lifespan of daf-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutants. We found that mitochondrial membrane potential exhibits a small but significant decrease in day 1 daf-2 mutants but a much greater decrease in day 8 daf-2 worms. We also examined the effect of genes and compounds that have been shown to alter mitochondrial membrane potential on daf-2 lifespan. Disruption of ucp-4, which increases mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased daf-2 lifespan without reducing wild-type longevity. Treatment with the mitochondrial uncoupling compound FCCP (carbonyl cyanide-p-trimethoxyphenylhydrazone), which decreases mitochondrial membrane potential, also decreased the longevity of daf-2 worms with no effect on wild-type lifespan. Combined, these results suggest that the altered mitochondrial membrane potential in daf-2 mutants contributes to their extended longevity and that their long lifespan is dependent on maintaining mitochondrial membrane potential within an optimum range.

title: Optimization of mitochondrial membrane potential contributes to extended longevity of daf-2 mutants in C. elegans
